text:
alex: Hey — planning to migrate `payments-api` from NLB (TLS passthrough) to an ALB with TLS termination + SNI routing so we can host multiple certs and do path-based routing. Quick checklist: what TF and k8s changes should I make?

samira: +1 good idea. main things: ALB expects HTTP/HTTPS target groups (not TLS) unless you use TLS target groups. we'll want the k8s Service to be type LoadBalancer but we should avoid NodePort if possible.

alex: ok — currently Service is type: LoadBalancer with annotation to create an NLB and `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: tcp` for passthrough. So switch annotations to ALB ones? any terraform changes?

li: For AWS ALB via ingress-controller (aws-alb-ingress-controller / aws-load-balancer-controller) you'll:
- add Ingress/IngressClass + controller-managed ALB annotations (or use Gateway API)
- Service should stay ClusterIP (ingress will target pods via ip target type) or NodePort depending on controller config
- TF: update IAM role for the controller to allow ACM/ELB actions if not already. No need to change the EKS nodegroup TF unless you were creating NLB via external LB resource.

samira: Important: health checks. ALB target groups do HTTP health checks by default. Make sure your readinessProbe path responds (200) on that port. If your service speaks TLS internally, set `backend-protocol: HTTPS` on the target group via annotation or use target type ip with TLS only if you actually need encryption to pods.

alex: We don't need pod-level TLS for now. So plan is ALB terminates TLS and forwards HTTP to pods on port 8080. Any secrets/cert change?

jordan: We'll use ACM certs in us-west-2. The controller can reference an ACM ARN via annotation `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/certificate-arn`. Make sure the cert covers all hostnames or use SNI with multiple ingress rules referencing different cert ARNs. security: we need ticket to rotate private keys?

alex: Who owns the ACM certs? I saw a cert for payments.example.com under infra-acm.

samira: infra team manages the cert ARNs in TF (aws_acm_certificate). We can export the ARN to SSM Parameter Store and the ingress controller can read it via annotation from a k8s secret OR you can hardcode the ARN in the ingress manifest (not ideal). Better: add `annotations` in our TF module that injects the ARN into k8s as a secret named `alb-certs` in ns `payments`.

li: Another pattern: use cert-manager with DNS-01 and let it provision certs to k8s secrets; controller supports referencing k8s cert secrets (if you're using cert-manager + alb-shim). But for ACM-backed ALB HTTPS listeners, the controller requires ACM ARN. cert-manager does not create ACM certs by default. Depends on what we want.

alex: We're leaning to keep ACM in TF since infra already has DNS and validation. Could you sketch the TF and k8s diff?

samira: TF diffs (high level):
- create/update aws_lb (ALB) resources? Actually controller creates ALBs for you; so update IAM role/mapping and export ACM ARNs to SSM
- add param /payments/acm_cert_arn -> value = aws_acm_certificate.payments.arn
- update controller IAM policy to allow `acm:DescribeCertificate` and `elasticloadbalancing:CreateListener` etc (should already exist)

k8s diffs (example):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: payments-ingress
  namespace: payments
  annotations:
    kubernetes.io/ingress.class: alb
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/scheme: internet-facing
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/listen-ports: '[{"HTTP":80},{"HTTPS":443}]'
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/certificate-arn: "arn:aws:acm:us-west-2:123456789012:certificate/..."
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/target-type: ip
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/backend-protocol: HTTP
spec:
  rules:
    - host: payments.example.com
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /payments
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: payments-svc
                port:
                  number: 8080
```
samira: And change the Service to ClusterIP (if target-type is ip) and ensure the controller can discover pod IPs. If you need stickiness, add annotations to enable cookie stickiness.

alex: Nice. What about weighted canary? We have an old NLB route for some customers — can we run ALB in parallel and shift a percentage?

li: ALB itself doesn't do weighted across ALBs. For gradual traffic split you can:
- DNS weighted routing (Route53 weighted records) between the NLB and ALB endpoints (fiddly)
- Or use a feature flag at app layer to route some users to ALB host header and keep NLB for others.
- Or teardown NLB and use ALB + target groups with different backend sets, but that won't help cross-LB split.

jordan: Security note: when ALB terminates TLS, ensure `X-Forwarded-Proto` is honored so app knows original scheme. Don't treat proxied traffic as internal only — keep client IP via `X-Forwarded-For` and set `externalTrafficPolicy` appropriately if you need source IP preserved. Using target-type ip usually preserves source via proxy protocol? Check docs.

samira: For preservation: with target-type ip, source IP in pod will be the client IP because ALB uses source NAT? Actually ALB is a proxy so X-Forwarded-For header is what you should rely on. NodePort/NLB with proxy protocol passes real client IP differently. So update app logging to read `X-Forwarded-For` for IPs.

alex: Got it. Any tf plan blockers you'd expect?

samira: Watch for existing NLB resources created outside controller. If NLB was created by service annotation previously, deleting/changing could remove the external ip and cause downtime. Plan to create ALB (controller) first and test with a unique host (staging.example.com) then flip DNS.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Reminder: when making IAM changes to the controller, schedule a rolling restart of the controller deployment to pick up new creds.

li: one more: if you use path-based routing and multiple hostnames, consider adding `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/success-codes` or tuning health check path to avoid 404s interfering.

alex: Thanks all — I'll draft a PR with: TF changes to export ACM ARN to SSM, k8s ingress manifest as above, change Service -> ClusterIP, update readiness probe path to /healthz. Will ping for code review.

samira: ping me when PR is ready, I'll review infra/TF bits.

jordan: I'll validate security checklist (TLS ciphers, ALB access logs, WAF) once PR is up.

alex: will do, thanks :thumbsup:
